What the differences mean

Why 16-inch, 16:10, 2560×1600 at 120 Hz is the line. Apple lists the 16-inch MacBook Pro's own screen as 16.2-inch, 3456×2234 at 254 ppi, with ProMotion up to 120 Hz. A 16-inch 2560×1600 panel has the same 16:10 shape and almost the same size, and at 120 Hz or more it keeps pace with ProMotion. Every row meets that line as its maker states it. Dealectric does not test units; the figures here come from the makers' pages and the named reviewers.

Left out for falling short of the line: 16-inch 1920×1200 extenders at 60 Hz such as the FOPO S11 (141.5 ppi); the Mobile Pixels Fold 16 QHD, which has a 2560×1600 panel but is listed at 220 cd/m² and carries no 120 Hz rating in the listing we hold; the 15.6-inch 3840×2160 espresso Pro, which Macworld lists at 60 Hz; and the ASUS ZenScreen MB16QHG, whose US spec page gives 2560×1600, 500 cd/m² and under 13 W but no refresh rate and no price on 2026-11-26.

The pick, the UPERFECT GR16EQ, is not sold by one of Dealectric's partner stores. It leads because it is the only row above 120 Hz and has the highest brightness figure a maker states. Prices were read on 2026-11-26 in Black Friday week; neither UPERFECT's nor SOTSU's page states when its sale price ends.

  • Sharpness against the MacBook. √(2560² + 1600²) ÷ 16 in = 188.7 ppi (UPERFECT states 188.68); 188.7 ÷ 254 = 74% of the MacBook's pixel density. A 16-inch 1920×1200 panel is 2,264.2 ÷ 16 = 141.5 ppi, or 56%.
  • Battery on one cable. Apple's 99.6 Wh battery over its 17-hour wireless-web figure (M5 Pro) is 99.6 ÷ 17 = 5.9 W. Add a screen at a 12 W rating (both UPERFECT models): 99.6 ÷ (5.9 + 12) = about 5.6 hours. At SOTSU's 11 W maximum: 99.6 ÷ 16.9 = about 5.9 hours. At the 7.5 W a retailer lists for the Duex Float 2 Pro: 99.6 ÷ 13.4 = about 7.5 hours. These are estimates from rated power, not tests.
  • Charging through the screen. The Duex Float 2 Pro passes through 65 W. Apple's minimum recommended charging wattage for this laptop is 94 W: 65 ÷ 94 = 69%. Against the 140 W adapter in the box: 65 ÷ 140 = 46%.
  • Carry weight with the 4.7 lb MacBook (Apple). GR16DQ: 4.7 + 1.58 = 6.28 lb. GR16EQ: 4.7 + 1.66 or 2.3 = 6.36 to 7.0 lb, depending on which of UPERFECT's two figures holds. Duex Float 2 Pro: 4.7 + 2.9 = 7.6 lb. SOTSU with its base: 4.7 + 3.01 = 7.71 lb.

Which port and cable to use on a 16-inch MacBook Pro

Any of the three Thunderbolt 5 ports, with a USB-C cable. Apple lists the current 16-inch MacBook Pro (M5 Pro or M5 Max) with three Thunderbolt 5 (USB-C) ports that support DisplayPort, so these screens run as native displays with no display driver. The M5 Pro drives up to three external displays and the M5 Max up to four, each at up to 6K 60 Hz or 4K 144 Hz. A 2560×1600 panel at 120 Hz or 144 Hz has fewer pixels than 4K at 144 Hz, so it sits inside that limit. For an older machine, Apple's page for the 2021 16-inch model gives two external displays on M1 Pro and four on M1 Max; check Apple's spec page for the 2023 and 2024 models.

Not the HDMI port. Steam Flow, in a review hosted on UPERFECT's blog, found the GR16EQ's mini HDMI input 'caps out at 130 Hz at this resolution' and that the full 144 Hz needs USB-C. For variable refresh, Apple's instruction is to connect an Adaptive Sync display to a Thunderbolt port with a Thunderbolt, USB-C or other DisplayPort-enabled cable, and it adds: 'Do not use an HDMI cable or adapter.' The setting is in System Settings, Displays, Refresh Rate. Apple also says to check Adaptive Sync compatibility with the display's maker. UPERFECT's page lists FreeSync but makes no statement about Macs, and Steam Flow's test ran on a Steam Deck.

Charge by MagSafe 3. The MacBook has a separate MagSafe 3 port for its 140 W adapter, so the charger does not need to pass through the monitor and all three Thunderbolt ports stay free. That makes the Duex Float 2 Pro's 65 W pass-through a convenience for light work, not the charging path for this laptop.

Plug in the screen's own power adapter for full brightness. On bus power from a Steam Deck, Steam Flow found the GR16EQ 'will default to 30% brightness every single time' and needed its charging brick for full brightness and saved settings; it drew 5 to 6.5 W in that state. UPERFECT includes a power adapter in the box. The 450 cd/m² figure is UPERFECT's own. Teoh Yi Chie at Parkablogs measured 238 nits on UPERFECT's 2023 UPlays C2 against 400 advertised, so treat the brightness column as makers' claims. The one screen of this type with a named measurement is the ASUS ZenScreen MB16QHG: Monitornerds measured 481 cd/m² against ASUS's 500.

Expect to adjust scaling. SOTSU's own page tells Mac users: 'To fix the macOS scaling issue, try BetterDisplay (third-party software).' Teoh Yi Chie wrote the same of the UPlays C2: 'MacOS users will need an app called BetterDisplay for proper (sharp) UI scaling.' All four rows share the 2560×1600 resolution this applies to.
